research_updates.title: Investment audit — two facility proposals retained without relabeling them as spend
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Business Oregon LTREZ structured data and attachments; City budgets, development agreements and planning packets; Apple releases; assessor values; permit records; contractor pages; SEC EDGAR. Retained: DC No. 1 proposed investment $250,000,000 at 2012-04-12 certification and DC No. 2 proposed investment $226,400,000 at 2016-02-25 certification, both campus/facility scope, unallocated, source projections. Boundaries: the required minima were $8.5 million and $200 million; proposed investment is not realized spend, assessed value, permit valuation or selected-building cost. Adversarial fourth pass repeated exact Apple Inc./Prineville/DC No. 1/DC No. 2 searches in Socrata resource re77-krua and all 2016-2025 attachments, City Ordinances 1195/1219 and Resolutions 1571/1573, the assessor's 15 Apple matches, ePermitting's 1600 Bal address inventory, and Apple EDGAR filings; none disclosed realized Prineville capex. Indispensable missing input: an audited facility/phase expenditure ledger with payment or placed-in-service dates and a crosswalk to IM3 building 00397914434.

research_updates.title: Adversarial fourth-pass disposition — direct series and narrow model inputs separated
research_updates.notes: Direct addition: Crook account 19494/R supplied ten exact tax-year 2016-2025 payment rows, receipts 238920-444833, retained only at single-account/company-county scope. Corrective model inputs: the latest $31,334.07 payment supports only a same-account service-cost break-even identity; the 100-job 2018 snapshot and BLS Central Oregon wages support only payroll occupation sensitivity; 267 million FY2025 campus kWh support an average-load conversion plus EIA price and EPA eGRID factor sensitivities. Investment still requires an audited Prineville facility/phase capex ledger and IM3 crosswalk. Construction requires original permit IDs, final nonoverlapping valuations, dates, worker-hours/payroll/residence and contractor tiers. Suppliers require paid invoices/contracts, vendor addresses and phase tags. Net fiscal requires the other 14 Apple account histories, treasurer reconciliation/distribution, same-scope service costs and building mapping. Community requires recipient-confirmed amount/quantity/value, date, purpose and attribution. County employment, wages and GDP require a dated Apple phase treatment series, defensible exposure share and comparison/counterfactual separating Meta and later Apple phases. Footprint allocation, minimum staffing, multiplier and before-after substitutes remain rejected because they would create false precision.

research_updates.title: Corrective modeling audit — five narrow sensitivities retained; causal and allocation candidates rejected
research_updates.notes: Investment: rejected — attempted anchors were DC No. 1/2 proposals, exempt values, assessor values and permits; none establishes realized spend or a selected-building allocation, so a bound would be misleading. Construction: rejected — attempted original-address permits and contractor pages lack a nonoverlapping original-building ledger, worker count, duration and payroll. Suppliers: rejected — attempted named contractors and CCB 69988 establish identity, not payments, local ownership or geography. Operations: retained only as a $4.372 million/$7.730 million/$11.800 million payroll sensitivity from the reported 100 jobs and 2018 BLS all-occupation/computer-math/CIS-manager wages; it is not observed or local payroll because FTE, employer, occupation and residence are unknown. Fiscal: net result rejected — account 19494, company bill, abatements and ASR SDC have incompatible scopes and incomplete recipient/cost coverage. Public costs: retained only as the $31,334.07 tax-year 2025 same-account break-even identity; actual service cost and net fiscal position remain unknown. Resources: retained FY2025 average load 30.479 MW from 267 million kWh; retained $21.494 million/$22.108 million/$28.195 million EIA price sensitivity after PacifiCorp Schedule 748 plus Schedules 294-296/2025 TAM proved noncomputable without voltage, capacity, demand, reactive power, adjustments, direct-access election/enrollment vintage and ESS price; retained 44,204.84-76,936.65 metric tons CO2e EPA eGRID geographic-factor sensitivity while preserving Apple's 100 percent renewable market claim. Water and selected-building allocations rejected for no meter/crosswalk. Community: rejected — attempted recipient pages lack monetary confirmation. County employment: rejected; County wages: rejected; County GDP: rejected — multiple Apple phases and Meta's campus defeat treatment isolation. Modeled additions: five; direct forecasts remain four.

interval.interpretation: Low applies EPA's Oregon state-generation total-output CO2e rate; central/high apply EPA's NWPP/WECC Northwest subregion total-output CO2e rate. modeled_syntheses.confidence_rationale: The energy input and EPA factors are public, but the factor vintage predates FY2025, Oregon production and NWPP consumption-region factors differ substantially, and no source reconciles them to Apple's contractual instruments or reporting boundary.
modeled_syntheses.decision_relevance: Shows the order of magnitude and geographic-factor sensitivity of grid-average location-based emissions while keeping Apple's renewable procurement claim separate.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Apple site-level location- and market-based Scope 2 inventory; contractual instrument attributes and retirement; hourly generation matching; utility loss treatment; exact eGRID subregion confirmation for every meter; FY2025 grid factor

derivation.formula: 267,000 MWh × eGRID total-output lb CO2e/MWh ÷ 2,204.62262185 lb/metric ton
assumptions: Oregon state output and NWPP subregion total-output rates are alternative location-based geographic benchmarks.

The NWPP factor is used as the central value because regional grid-average factors are more appropriate to consumption context than a state production factor; the Oregon factor is retained only to expose geographic-factor sensitivity.
No grid-loss uplift, marginal/non-baseload factor, avoided-emissions credit or renewable-contract adjustment is applied.
Apple's 100 percent renewable-electricity statement is a market/procurement claim and is not overwritten by this location-based sensitivity.

limitations: The range is driven by factor choice and is not a true-value bound.
eGRID2023 factors do not match Apple FY2025 exactly.
This is not an audited GHG Protocol inventory and must not be reported as Apple's Scope 2 emissions.
The model does not contradict or quantify Apple's separately reported 100 percent renewable-electricity procurement claim.
The campus result cannot be allocated to the selected building.
modeled_syntheses.notes: Location-based grid-average sensitivity only. Central equals high because no more emissions-intensive location-based total-output factor was defensible; the non-baseload factor was rejected as a marginal rather than location-based accounting measure.

legacy_first_entry_note: Apple reports that its Prineville data center opened in May 2012, but Facebook publicly identified its first dedicated Prineville data center on April 7, 2011. The Apple candidate cannot be Crook County's first entry; a complete historical inventory remains unestablished.

project_description: Apple's Prineville data-center project is an Apple-operated campus at 1600 SW Baldwin Road in Prineville, Crook County, Oregon; the selected IM3 object is one mapped 9,228-square-foot building, not the entire campus. Apple reports that the Prineville data center has used 100 percent renewable electricity since opening in May 2012, while public planning material describes three much larger campus buildings developed through 2023. Business Oregon separately labels two enterprise-zone facilities DC No. 1 and DC No. 2, and none of those campus or facility totals is allocated to the selected building.
